messages:
Maria Chen: Quick intake — customer X asked for deterministic response routing so their SLAs don't spike during model fallbacks. Problem: when the primary model overloads we currently route to a cheaper variant which changes output distribution and breaks their downstream scoring. Need: proposal for a rollout that minimizes quality regression while meeting 99th pctl latency targets.
Sean Patel: Can you paste the customer example and their current traffic profile?
Maria Chen: TL;DR: 20% of requests are high-priority (scored offline), 80% are interactive. Peak qps 450, p99 target 300ms. They see wrong scoring when we switch to smaller model. Example failure attached (short prompt -> different class).
Arjun Iyer: Two immediate levers: (1) sticky routing with cached KV for hot prefixes, (2) canary mode where a sample of requests is duplicated for the cheaper model to estimate distribution shift. Both have perf/cost tradeoffs.
Ella Gomez: Customer is sensitive to changes — legal requires stability for scoring output. They prefer conservative rollouts.
Priya Nair: Proposed goals: reduce SLA breaches during overloads to <0.5% monthly, keep scoring parity within delta-auc of 0.01 vs baseline, and cap cost uplift to +20% for M1. Non-goals: full model retraining or changing customer scoring logic.
Sean Patel: Acceptance criteria (engineering): 1) deterministic routing policy option that routes by tenant+priority, 2) fallback model only used when explicit capacity threshold reached, 3) telemetry: per-tenant change-rate metric + distribution drift alert.
Arjun Iyer: Edge cases: tenant burst that saturates dedicated pool, cold prefixes with no KV cache, and multi-tenant collocated hosts where fallback causes noisy neighbor effects. Will need admission control + tenant isolation knob.
Maria Chen: Risks: having two live models increases test surface; We need an eval harness to detect semantic drift automatically before we declare rollout pass.
Priya Nair: Success metrics (product): - Monthly SLA breach rate <0.5% - Delta AUC <= 0.01 on sampled scoring set - % requests served by primary model during peak >= 85% - Rollout false positive alerts <= 2 per month
Ella Gomez: Customer asks for audit log entries showing which model served each request (for compliance). Also wants monthly report comparing pre/post distributions.
Sean Patel: Implementation sketch: Phase 1 (MVP) = deterministic routing config + model-tagging in logs + sampling dupes for offline eval. Phase 2 = adaptive admission control + KV prefix caching + canary traffic mirroring.
Arjun Iyer: Est. effort: M1 ~ 3 sprints (eng-runtime: 2, eng-platform: 1) for routing + telemetry + log tagging. M2 ~ 4–5 sprints for caching + admission + auto-rollbacks.
Maria Chen: Proposed scope negotiation: offer M1 as paid integration for Dedicated or Private customers with SLA; M2 as follow-up. That keeps Hosted rollout simpler. Thoughts?
Priya Nair: Sounds reasonable. We should capture explicit non-goals for Hosted: no tenant-level dedicated pools initially.
Sean Patel: Agree. Also need decision on evaluation thresholds (what triggers auto-rollback). Suggest: semantic-drift alert when sampled delta-auc >0.015 OR per-tenant customer complaint spike >2x baseline.
Ella Gomez: I'll confirm with customer legal on audit format and reporting cadence.
DevBot: Reminder: Quarterly roadmap sync slot booked Thu 10:00 — added this thread to agenda.
Maria Chen: Next steps: I'll draft a short PRD with problem statement, M1/M2 scope, acceptance criteria, and implementation estimate. Can folks review by EOD Friday?
Sean Patel: Yep, will review.
Arjun Iyer: I'll add runtime constraints and a short runbook for rollback conditions.
Ella Gomez: I'll collect the customer's example prompts and scoring set (sanitized).
Priya Nair: I'll draft the success metric dashboard and evaluations we need.
Maria Chen: Thanks — leaving the doc stub in /docs/rdx/prd-routing-intake (will ping).
